beats.say: Flipping twenty eight heads in a row is more likely than winning the Powerball jackpot.
Every step adds a zero to the odds. Rolling a six on one die: one in six.
Getting struck by lightning in your lifetime: about one in fifteen thousand.
A royal flush in five cards: about one in six hundred and fifty thousand.
Twenty eight heads in a row: one in two hundred and sixty eight million.
The Powerball jackpot: one in two hundred and ninety two million. Even worse than the coin.
Dealt all thirteen spades in a bridge hand? One in six hundred and thirty five billion.
So next time you buy a ticket, try flipping a coin first.
Follow Ship With Pip for more.

title: 28 heads in a row is more likely than winning Powerball
caption: Each step adds a zero to the odds. Rolling a six: 1 in 6. Struck by lightning in your lifetime: about 1 in 15,300 (National Weather Service). A royal flush in a 5 card deal: 4 out of 2,598,960 hands, 1 in 649,740. 28 heads in a row: 1 in 2^28 = 1 in 268,435,456. Powerball jackpot: 1 in 292,201,338, so it is less likely than 28 heads in a row. All 13 spades in a 13 card bridge hand: 1 in 635,013,559,600.
facts: royal flush = C(52,5)/4 = 2,598,960/4 = 649,740; 2^28 = 268,435,456 < 292,201,338 (Powerball, powerball.com); all spades = C(52,13) = 635,013,559,600. Steps (first n with 10^n >= odds): six 1, lightning 15,300 -> 5, royal 6, 28 heads 9, Powerball 9, spades 12.
